comparator.name: International Land and Water Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: a 117-EC named compulsory common part, a 3-EC mathematics/statistics restricted choice, an 18-EC internship, a 12-EC thesis and 30 EC of open electives. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected by the official-order tie-break. Current programme material confirms the integrated biophysical, socio-economic, policy and design identity.
components: Exploring Professional Practices in International Land and Water Management
Orientation on International Land & Water Management
Design in Land and Water Management 1
Economic and Sociological Analysis of Rural Livelihoods
Design in Land and Water Management 2
Research Methodology for Human Environment Interactions
Selected by official-order tie-break from the 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice.
BSc Internship International Land and Water Management
BSc Thesis International Land and Water Management
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.label: Land, water & integrated sustainability
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible programme integrating land, water, climate and ecosystems with economics, community and governance perspectives for sustainable resource management.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines earth and environmental systems, water, ecology, climate, economics, data, governance and applied sustainability research.
progression: Sustainability, earth-system, ecology, economics and data foundations precede land, water, environmental analysis, governance and applied research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Climate, water & geospatial resilience
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced drought, flood, climate-adaptation, GIS and disaster-resilience direction through climate science, water systems, earth observation, spatial data and environmental research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres climate, hazards, water, earth observation, spatial data, soils, environmental systems and applied resilience research.
progression: Earth-system, water, climate, ecology and data foundations precede earth observation, environmental systems, spatial analysis and advanced resilience research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes climate hazards, water systems and geospatial evidence the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by at least five courses and 37.5 EC.

alternatives.label: Land, water & sustainability governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines environmental systems and water with institutions, politics, economics, law, environmental justice, communication and policy research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced governance and community direction through land-water institutions, environmental justice, economics, law, public policy, stakeholder communication and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes institutions, environmental justice, economics, law and community governance the organising priority. It differs from both environmental-science-led programmes by well over four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Sustainability, sociology, politics, economics, data and environmental foundations precede law, public economics, resource governance, environmental justice and applied research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.

core: Land, water, soils, hydrology and environmental processes
Climate change, drought, flooding, erosion and adaptation
Agriculture, irrigation, land degradation and sustainable resource management
Communities, livelihoods, economics, policy and land-water politics
Engineering, GIS, field research, design and human-environment methods
adjacent: Land-water governance, livelihoods and environmental justice
questions: How can land and water systems be managed under drought, flooding and climate change?
How can environmental science, engineering and social knowledge support fair resource decisions?
How do spatial evidence, institutions and communities shape resilient landscapes?

candidates.label: Geography education
candidates.reason: Geography education is a valid direction, but the three-alternative maximum is reached and UCR does not provide a teacher-qualification pathway; spatial and environmental geography content is already represented.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates land, water, environmental science and society. Climate/geospatial resilience and land-water governance support two further coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct directions. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated international land-and-water curriculum with hydrology, hydraulics, irrigation, soils, engineering design, field practice, an internship and a thesis. UCR can combine substantial environmental science, water, spatial analysis, economics and governance, but it does not reproduce the same professional land-and-water engineering sequence.
